verdicts.proposal_name: P1: Restore/overshoot the idiosyncratic cash-flow band (0.1 -> 1.75) + ivol characteristic
verdicts.critique:
I re-ran this from scratch (BGN create_arrays with the `0.1*0.3` at panel_functions_bgn.py:54 patched to `MULT*0.3`, real sdf_compute_bgn.sdf_loop, N=250, T=180, seed 7, months 150/160/170/175) and I have to report three things.

FIRST, A METHODOLOGICAL CORRECTION THAT CUTS IN THE PROPOSER'S FAVOUR. The prior BGN-diagnosis agent's span numbers (the '91.7% for {1,size,bm}' family) used `P_{col(L^{-1}X)}` with z=L^{-1}rp. That projector is WRONG. With Sigma=LL', w'Sigma w = ||L'w||^2, so the span is col(L^T X), not col(L^{-1}X). I verified against brute-force optimisation and against the closed form sqrt(rp'X(X'Sigma X)^{-1}X'rp): on a random 40x5 test the wrong formula gives 0.0174 and the right one 0.00580 = brute force. The proposer used the correct formula. So the baseline headroom is genuinely larger than the diagnosis brief says.

SECOND, THE POPULATION CLAIM REPRODUCES, WITH A HAIRCUT. At m=0.1: {1,logmve,bm} attains 0.882-0.909 of max SR, +log(true ivol) 0.911-0.952, quadratic 0.973-0.984. At m=1.75: {1,logmve,bm} 0.728-0.739 (proposer said 0.691), +log(true ivol) 0.749-0.774 (proposer 0.720), quadratic 0.912-0.946 (proposer 0.935). So the ceiling ratio is 1.22-1.25x, not 1.30x. Directionally the proposer is right and I could not refute the population mechanism.

THIRD, AND THIS IS THE KILL SHOT: THE MECHANISM IS UNMEASURABLE AND UNLEARNABLE AT m=1.75. (a) The characteristic that is supposed to make 1/d learnable does not measure d. Regressing the 60-month trailing realized return sd on the true conditional sd at the same date gives corr = 0.111 (t=150) and 0.146 (t=170), i.e. R^2 = 1-2%. A 36-month window gives 0.015-0.137; a 120-month window gives 0.124-0.236. Substituting the FEASIBLE 60-month ivol for the true one collapses the quadratic basis from 0.912/0.924 to 0.804/0.835 and leaves the linear basis at 0.728/0.740. The realised nonlinearity ratio is therefore 1.10x, not 1.30x. (b) The reason is that at m=1.75 sigma_j runs to 3.87, so a single project's cash flow is a lognormal with CV = sqrt(exp(sigma^2)-1) averaging 121 (baseline: 4.35). No finite window estimates the variance of such a variable. (c) Consequently the model's own conditional second moment is a number the data never shows: mean diag(cond_var) at t=170 is 0.03733 (19.3%/mo) while the average realised cross-sectional variance over 59 months is 0.00482 (6.9%/mo) - a factor of 7.7 in variance. At m=0.1 the same two numbers are 0.00333 and 0.00400, i.e. consistent. So at m=1.75 the metric grades every method against a covariance matrix whose dispersion is carried by tail mass that never realises in the estimator's 360-month training sample. (d) The calibration targets are not actually hit in the object a data user would measure: pooled realised monthly return sd is 7.4% (not 12.3%), realised excess kurtosis is 149 and skewness +3.8, and median conditional sd is 10.7% while sqrt(mean cond var) is 19.3% - the '12.3%/month matches CRSP' claim is an artefact of averaging a variance whose mean is dominated by a handful of firms.

FOURTH, CODE: the 'exact change' list is wrong. fama_functions.py:63 has its OWN hardcoded `_CHAR_TO_FACTOR = {bm,agr,roe,mom,mkt_lev}` and line 65-... does `factor_dct[name_dct[char]]`. Adding 'ivol' to chars raises `KeyError: 'ivol'` - I ran it. config.CHAR_TO_FACTOR (config.py:229) is dead code; nothing imports it (grep confirms only config.py references it). So the prescribed config edit is a no-op and the FF leg crashes; the tempting 'fix' of leaving ivol out of FF's char list would hand DKKM a strictly larger information set and make any DKKM-over-FF gap an artefact.

FIFTH, ARITHMETIC. max_sr falls 0.27 -> 0.21/month, a 21% cut, so every method's signal-to-noise per managed portfolio falls by 21% while return volatility roughly triples. In basis points: the FEASIBLE ceiling gap is (0.82-0.74)*0.21 = 1.7 percentage points of monthly Sharpe = 0.06 annualised, against a real-data target gap of FF 0.74 -> DKKM 1.93-2.50 annualised.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM cannot form b(x)/d(x) - that part is airtight and I confirm it (adding log ivol linearly buys FM only 2-3 points). But FF is NOT as helpless as the proposal says: fama_french value-weights within every cell (fama_functions.py:88-93, and mkt_rf = mve/mve.sum() at line 115), so FF's weight space is {mve_i x step function of chars}, which is already nonlinear in chars. Since at high band d_i falls with project count and hence with size, FF's mechanical size tilt partly implements the 1/d tilt for free; my FF-style 4-column basis attains 0.64-0.71 of max at m=1.75 versus 0.75-0.78 for FM-linear-with-true-ivol, so FF loses far less ground than the 'step functions cannot track a 4700x spread' argument implies. More importantly the gap is likely to be SMALLER than the population ceiling suggests, not larger, because (i) with the feasible ivol char the ceiling gap is 1.10x, (ii) the true w* down-weights high-sigma_j firms by up to 700x on the strength of tail variance the 360-month training sample never displays, so no estimator - DKKM included - will learn that down-weighting, and (iii) DKKM's second rank-standardization (dkkm_functions.py:110) forces every feature to the identical bounded uniform marginal, so DKKM structurally cannot produce a weight vector that is enormous on the low-d minority. The most likely realised outcome is that all three methods fall roughly proportionally and the ratio barely moves, while max_sr and HJD both degrade.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the diagnosis (idiosyncratic risk is far too small: sd(log d)=0.19, pairwise corr 0.54, idio share 0.51) but change the instrument. (1) Do NOT get dispersion from the lognormal exponent sigma_j, which produces CV=121 cash flows, exkurt 149, and a conditional variance 7.7x the realisable one. Instead put the dispersion in a firm-level, PERSISTENT, thin-tailed scale: give each FIRM a permanent idiosyncratic-volatility type (e.g. multiply the non-systematic component of eps by a firm-level lognormal with sd(log)=0.5, redrawn on a 10-year half-life), leaving sigma_j's band at m=1.0-1.25. That yields sd(log d) around 0.6-0.8 with realised kurtosis in single digits AND makes trailing realized vol an actual measurement of d (persistence of log d is only 0.52-0.71 over 30 months even now, so firm-level persistence is the binding requirement). (2) Verify measurability BEFORE claiming headroom: report corr(60-month realized vol, true conditional sd) and re-do the span calculation with the feasible char, not the true one. My run says that single substitution costs 11 percentage points of the quadratic ceiling. (3) Add a check that mean diag(cond_var) matches the average realised cross-sectional variance to within ~25%; if it does not, the metric is grading unlearnable tail variance. (4) Fix fama_functions.py:63 and :170 to read the mapping from config, and add ivol to FF's sorts, or the comparison is rigged.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2: Project-scale / intangible-capital wedge kappa breaking the rp = a + b/mve + Chat*pi*bm identity
verdicts.critique:
The premise is correct and I verified it from the code rather than the claim. eret[1:] = (term1+term2+term3+term4)/P - 1 (panel_functions_bgn.py:181-187) with term1 and term3 date-level scalars, term2 = pi*A*e_t and A = P - G (line 164), term4 = Chat*pi*book (line 181), book = I*num (line 144). So 1+eret_i = (term1+term3-pi*e_t*G_t)/P_i + pi*e_t + Chat*pi*bm_i exactly. rp is exactly affine in (1/mve, bm) with a bm coefficient of Chat*pi = 0.024476 at every date. Confirmed empirically: my span basis {1, 1/mve, bm} attains 0.884-0.912 of max SR at baseline, statistically identical to {1, log mve, bm}. So the diagnosis is right and P2 attacks a real degeneracy.

But the NONLINEARITY the proposal claims to create largely cancels. The whole DKKM-only content is the firm-specific shrinkage pi_i = s^2/(s^2 + noise_i^2/(num_i*H)) applied to the payout signal. Both terms scale as 1/num_i: the signal variance is s^2 = Var(Lambda_i/num_i) = (exp(sigma_kappa^2)-1)/num_i, and the noise variance of the averaged payout yield is CV^2/(num_i*H). Their ratio, hence pi_i, is INDEPENDENT of num_i to first order. The proposer's headline 'firm-specific shrinkage depending on project count' is therefore approximately constant in exactly the variable it names. What survives is only heterogeneity through per-project cash-flow CV, i.e. through ivol - a one-dimensional interaction, not the advertised three-way one.

Worse, the recommended stacking with P1 destroys the channel outright. At m=1.75 I measure mean per-project CV = 121. With num=6 and a 60-month payout average, the noise variance of y relative to the signal mean is 121^2/(6*60) = 40.7, against a signal variance of (exp(0.75^2)-1)/6 = 0.128. R^2 of the payout characteristic on the latent Lambda/mve is 0.128/(0.128+40.7) = 0.003. The signal is dead, so the optimal shrinkage is zero for every firm and there is no heterogeneity left to exploit. At baseline (CV=4.35) the same calculation gives R^2 = 0.71 and the channel is alive - so P1 and P2 are mutually destructive, which is the opposite of the proposer's 'stacked 1.6-2.0x'.

Finally, the risk assessment understates the code hazard: kappa has to be inserted in eight distinct places in sdf_compute_bgn.py (col1, col3 but NOT col2 which is exponentiated; three diagonal corrections; the term2t option-times-option correction with E[kappa^2]; and the term4 kron). A single misplacement silently biases cond_var with no exception raised - the exact failure mode already documented for kp14's integ_results.npz. There is no unit test in the repo that would catch it.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM given a payout characteristic captures the constant-shrinkage projection E[Lambda/mve | y] = pi_bar*y + const, and because the MVE step itself chooses the coefficient on the payout factor, FM automatically attains the OPTIMAL CONSTANT shrinkage. So FM loses only Var((pi_i - pi_bar)*y_i), and I have just argued the dominant driver of pi_i heterogeneity (num_i) cancels. FF is less crippled than claimed too: its 2x3 sorts are size x payout with value weighting, which is precisely a two-level size-dependent loading on the payout signal - a coarse version of the interaction. And note num_i is not an unobserved state: num = book/I = bm*mve/I, so it is an exact function of two characteristics FM already has, which means any 'interaction with project count' that did survive could be handed to FM as one extra column (bm*mve*payout) by a referee in one line. The honest expected gap from this channel is a few percent, not 1.2-1.35x.
verdicts.salvage: Keep kappa (it is the right target - it breaks a genuine algebraic degeneracy and it does not touch Jstar or the exercise rule) but drive the shrinkage heterogeneity through a variable whose SIGNAL does not scale with it. Firm age / history length H_i does exactly that: pi_i = s^2/(s^2 + CV^2/(num_i*H_i)) with s^2 proportional to 1/num_i gives pi_i = 1/(1 + CV^2/(s0^2*H_i)) - monotone in H_i, with no cancellation. Age is not currently in MODEL_CHARS and is a genuinely non-redundant observable. So: sigma_kappa = 0.5, keep the band at m<=1.25 so the payout signal has R^2 around 0.5-0.7, add `age` and payout at 12/60/120-month horizons as characteristics, and let the nonlinearity be shrinkage-in-age times payout. Also add a brute-force Monte Carlo validation of ER (simulate R_{t+1} at a fixed t and compare the sample second moment elementwise to sdf_loop's ER) before trusting any result.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3: Repair agr, add observable characteristics, rescale GAMMA_GRID by sqrt(130/L)
verdicts.critique:
The hygiene half is right and worth doing; the bandwidth half is wrong for BGN and the implementation instructions are incorrect.

WHAT IS RIGHT: agr really is degenerate (book = I*num at panel_functions_bgn.py:144 is a small integer), so `x.pct_change()` on it is 91% ties at zero, rank_standardize's np.argsort (dkkm_functions.py:57-62) turns the tied mass into a persistent pseudo-random column, and fama_french's tercile split at q30=q70=0 produces literally empty medium portfolios. Replacing with 12-month book growth is free and unambiguously correct. NMAT=5 -> 1 and a denser alpha grid are also correct and, per the pipeline audit already in the brief, more consequential than anything else on the estimator side.

WHAT IS WRONG: (1) The prescribed config edit does nothing. fama_functions.py:63 and :170 each hold their own hardcoded `_CHAR_TO_FACTOR`; config.py:229 CHAR_TO_FACTOR is referenced nowhere outside config.py (verified by grep). Adding 'ivol'/'payout'/'age' to MODEL_CHARS['bgn'] makes fama_french raise `KeyError: 'ivol'` - I ran it and it does. fama_macbeth survives only because line 172 uses `.get(c, c)`. So as written the change breaks the FF leg, and the only silent 'fix' (give FF fewer chars) manufactures a DKKM-over-FF gap out of an information-set asymmetry.
(2) The bandwidth rescale is not supported and is probably harmful here. My span computation says the ACTUAL configured RFF basis is not the constraint: on rank-standardized (log mve, bm, log ivol) at m=1.75, RFF with D=36 already attains 0.914-0.951 of max SR and D=360 attains 1.0000 (trivially, since D exceeds N). At production N=1000 with D=3600, the RFF span is R^N and the population ceiling is 1.0 for ANY DGP. So every 'population span ceiling' argument in this proposal set is vacuous for the largest DKKM model - the entire question is estimation efficiency, and widening gamma raises the number of reachable directions per fixed feature budget, which is exactly what you do not want when the truth is low-order. The brief's own independent experiment (x8 rescale: 0.157 vs 0.254 with a linear truth) says the same.
(3) The proposal is honest that it is worth 1.02-1.05x alone. As a mechanism it is not one.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: By the proposer's own admission, no. And the asymmetry arguments are weaker than stated: adding chars enlarges FM's linear span one-for-one and FM is already realising ~97% of its own population ceiling (realised FM 0.2357 vs a population linear ceiling of ~0.89*0.27 = 0.24), so every clean new linear direction goes almost entirely to FM. Repairing agr helps FF as much as it helps DKKM (it un-empties FF's cma medium portfolios). The one genuinely DKKM-only knob, gamma, I have just argued should be left alone. Net expected movement in the DKKM/FF ratio: within noise of zero.
verdicts.salvage: Ship the subset that is pure hygiene and defensible independent of any model change: (a) 12-month agr; (b) fix fama_functions.py:63 and :170 to read config.CHAR_TO_FACTOR so FF and FM see the same characteristics, and add an assertion that len(factor_names) == number of FF columns; (c) NMAT = 1 with the 5 draws reported as replications; (d) replace ALPHA_LST with a grid that visits effective df in (63, 360), e.g. [0, 3e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2, 1e-1, 1]; (e) propagate max_sr from *_moments.pkl into results.pkl and report Sharpe/max_sr - without it nobody can tell a failing estimator from an empty model. Hold gamma and the extra characteristics until a model change with a demonstrably nonlinear, MEASURABLE target exists, and then re-derive the bandwidth empirically rather than from sqrt(130/L).

verdicts.proposal_name: P4: Cohort (vintage) common cash-flow factors, unpriced, with age-dependent exposures
verdicts.critique:
The load-bearing argument is a dimension count - 'FM's achievable cohort-exposure vectors form an L-dimensional subspace of a K_eff-dimensional exposure space, so FM attains at most sqrt(L/K_eff)' - and it is wrong for UNPRICED factors. Adding an unpriced common factor does not create a Sharpe gap between spans in proportion to dimension count; it adds variance that must be diversified, and diversification is a 1/N effect, not a 1/K_eff effect. The brief's own oracle experiment makes this point in the general case (under exact factor pricing at N=1000, equal-weight attains 99.81% of max SR; the analytic shortfall is 1/(2*sigma_f^2*beta'D^{-1}beta) ~ 0.19%). Concretely here: a firm holds ~6 live projects (my sim: mean num 5.9), so with RHO_COH=0.78 and K_eff~24 a firm loads on ~6 of 24 cohorts with weight ~1/6 each. A portfolio spread over N=1000 firms has cohort-m exposure approximately (1/N)*sum_i phi_m(i) ~ 1/24, so total cohort variance is ~sigma_coh^2/24 - already 24x diversified before any hedging. The residual that a rich basis could hedge and a linear basis could not is a second-order slice of that.

The proposal also has a fatal dependency chain: it states it REQUIRES P1 (without the wide band there is only ~7% non-systematic cash-flow variance to allocate), and A0_COH = 0.37 is calibrated off P1's variance decomposition. I have just shown P1 at m=1.75 produces CV=121 lognormal cash flows and a conditional variance 7.7x the realisable one. Layering a cohort factor on top of that means the cohort factor's contribution to the TRUE cond_var is also carried by unrealisable tail mass. And max_sr falls further (unpriced variance added to the denominator), so the numbers being compared shrink.

The implementation risk is real and the proposer names it: the cohort kernel enters as a per-ROW multiplier on kron(col2v, col2v) with row = s*(t+1)+s', and getting the index mapping wrong silently produces a wrong covariance with no exception - the same silent-corruption class as kp14's integ_results.npz and the P_down_diff self-reference bug in loadings_compute_gs21.py:29-32. Plus a 15-20% runtime hit on a moments step already pinned to n_jobs=1.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Even granting the mechanism, FM captures most of it once `age` is a characteristic - which this proposal requires anyway. Firm i's cohort-exposure profile phi(i) is, in expectation, a smooth function of age (zero above the firm's age, rising, then geometrically decaying with the pi=0.99 survival rate), so a linear-in-age hedge already removes the leading component of the exposure and a linear-in-(age, age^2) hedge removes the next. FF's size x age double sort with value weighting adds a coarse second dimension. And the residual bump structure is precisely what diversifies at rate 1/sqrt(number of firms per cohort) ~ 1/sqrt(42) at N=1000. The proposer's own honest note - 'this is my least certain magnitude... if that concentration is weak the gain is at the low end' - is the right read, and the pre-implementation diagnostic they suggest (regress the true MVE weight on the age profile; check the FM-span-optimal portfolio's implied cohort exposure) should be run first and will, I predict, come back near zero.
verdicts.salvage: Make the cohort/sector factors PRICED. That is the same code change (the cohort shock already enters eps at panel_functions_bgn.py:69-76) with one difference: let the vintage/sector shock v_m be correlated with the pricing kernel, so cov(log M, log C_j) = -(beta_j + theta_m(j)) and the risk-neutral project value becomes Chat*exp(-beta_j - theta_{m(j)}). Jstar.csv and the exercise rule survive if you fold theta into an equivalent beta shift, so no solution file is re-solved. This attacks the ACTUAL binding blocker identified everywhere in the diagnosis - BGN has exactly ONE priced shock and a rank-1 price-of-risk vector, EffRank(E[FF']) ~ 2 versus the several hundred that DKKM's AIPT calibration requires - rather than adding unpriced variance that diversifies away. Twenty priced sector shocks with heterogeneous, characteristic-dependent loadings is the single change with the best theoretical case in the whole set, and it is no harder to code than the unpriced version.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5: Characteristic-dependent clientele demand wedge (an AIPT alpha)
verdicts.critique:
I cannot refute the core of this one, and I should say so plainly. Every other proposal leaves BGN a frictionless economy in which mu = -cov(R, m) by construction, and the brief's own oracle span experiment settles what that implies: with exact factor pricing the RFF-over-linear ceiling ratio is 0.994 at N=1000, and it only exceeds 2x once a non-covariance premium component exists. My own numbers agree - at baseline the true MVE weight is spread over an effective 105 of 199 firms and the linear span attains ~0.89 of max, so there is nothing large to win. P5 is the only proposal that changes the sign of the theoretical answer.

But four things must change.

(1) THE WEDGE LEAKS INTO THE LINEAR SPAN THROUGH MOMENTUM, AND FM WILL EAT IT. log W_{i,t+1} = theta*h(x_it) + u_{i,t+1} with u an AR(1) at rho_u = 0.97 is, mechanically, a slow mean-reverting valuation error. That makes past returns linearly predictive of future returns, and `mom` (panel_functions_bgn.py:249-251) and `bm` (which is I*num/(P*W), so the wedge is literally in the denominator of book-to-market) are already characteristics. So a large fraction of the alpha will show up as an ordinary linear value/reversal effect that FM's monthly cross-sectional regression captures exactly. Orthogonalising h against the contemporaneous char columns does NOT fix this, because the leakage comes from u, not from h. You must either set rho_u near zero (killing the limits-to-arbitrage story) or orthogonalise the realised wedge path, not just its target.

(2) THE ORTHOGONALISATION IS CIRCULAR. The chars are functions of the wedge-contaminated price (bm = book/(P*W), size = log(P*W)), so h(x_t) is orthogonal to chars that themselves depend on W_{t-1}. This is a fixed point, and the sign of the residual dependence is not obvious. Worse, 'orthogonalise h against the char columns each month' means the result is true by construction and a referee will say so - the proposer concedes this. The defensible version is a structural segmented-clientele demand system where the orthogonality is an outcome, not an input.

(3) THE METRICS BREAK AT THE TARGET CALIBRATION. At S* ~ 1.1/month, sd(sdf_ret) = Rf*S*/(1+S*^2) collapses and E[sdf_ret] -> Rf, so HJD for every method converges toward ~0.7-0.75 and the whole between-method range is ~25% of the level. And the Sharpe metric is a mean-of-ratios over 360 months (create_slides_tables.py:34-42), which at alpha=0 with an interpolating ridge produces near-hedged w_t with tiny denominators; those months will dominate. Switch to sqrt(1 - rho_uncentered^2) and report the median and pooled Sharpe BEFORE running this, or the metric will hide the result.

(4) BLOW-UP RISK. sd(alpha) = 36bp/month against idiosyncratic vol that P1 would have raised to 10.5%/month means the true w* is alpha/d, and if this is stacked with P1's d spanning 250-700x (my measurement, not the proposer's 4715x), w* concentrates on a handful of low-d firms. My concentration diagnostic already shows the effective number of firms carrying the MVE falling from 105 to 76 at N=200 from P1 alone. Add alpha/d and it will fall much further, at which point max_sr is set by a few names, HJD is set by a few names, and DKKM's rank-standardized features (every column forced to the same bounded uniform marginal, dkkm_functions.py:110) structurally cannot express the required spike.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: The strongest case against it: FM 'cannot' capture h only because h has been defined orthogonal to a FIXED list of five characteristics. That is a statement about the char list, not about linear methods. A referee adds h's leading principal components - or just size*bm, size^2, bm^2 - as FM columns and the gap closes, because h is a deterministic function of the same five chars. DKKM's advantage here is not that it can see something FM cannot; it is that FM was handed a deliberately incomplete basis. In real data the analogous claim is defensible because nobody knows the functional form; in a simulation where the modeller chose h, it is not. Second: FF is less helpless than claimed - value-weighted 2x3 sorts give weights of the form mve x step, so an h built as a bump in small-value-high-vol space (the proposer's own suggested economic h) is substantially a size x value cell indicator, which is exactly what FF's double sort spans. Third: the reversal leakage in (1) hands a first-order share of alpha to FM for free.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the AIPT premium - it is the only ingredient that can close the 3-5x gap - but implement it so the orthogonality is earned. (a) Specify a segmented-clientele demand system: a fraction of wealth is held by investors with a mandate to hold a characteristic-tilted portfolio (e.g. benchmark-relative constraints), clear the market, and let the wedge be whatever the clearing condition produces. Do not orthogonalise by projection. (b) Make the wedge target depend on a LATENT, slowly-revealed state (e.g. an index-membership indicator that is a nonmonotone function of size history) rather than on a hand-chosen polynomial of the contemporaneous chars. (c) Set rho_u low enough, or add the wedge to a non-price object, so the alpha does not show up as ordinary reversal in `mom`. (d) Ship it standalone at baseline d, not stacked with P1, so the true MVE weight stays diversified over hundreds of firms; report the effective number of firms carrying max_sr as a guard. (e) Replace HJD with sqrt(1 - rho_unc^2) and report Sharpe/max_sr, median and pooled, before the first run.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6: Heterogeneous project durability (2-3 discrete survival types), re-solving Jstar
verdicts.critique:
This buys the least and costs the most, and the arithmetic is against it on its own terms.

The interest-rate factor it enriches is essentially unpriced. corr_zr = BETA_ZR/(SIGMA_Z*SIGMA_R) = -0.00014/(0.4*0.002) = -0.175 (config.py:200-205; the construction is at panel_functions_bgn.py:33-36), so lambda_xi = -0.070 against lambda_mu = +0.394 - the xi factor carries 3.1% of the squared price of risk. Hedging an almost-unpriced common factor better is worth O(1/N) of max Sharpe by the same diversification algebra that gives 0.19% at N=1000 in the brief's oracle experiment. The 9:1 variance ratio the proposal cites is a VARIANCE fact, not a premium fact, and the Sharpe metric is scale-invariant in w and only rewards rotation toward Sigma^{-1}rp.

If you instead raise BETA_ZR to -0.00044 to make the rate factor genuinely priced, then rp acquires a term linear in the firm's duration mix. A linear function of the type shares is in FM's span the moment any duration-informative characteristic is supplied, so the enrichment goes largely to FM. The proposal's own answer - that the mix must be identified only by a COMBINATION of signals with no single char ordering the types - is a request to hand-tune the type parameters until FM fails, which is the same 'assume the conclusion' objection levelled at P5 but with none of P5's theoretical payoff.

The proposal also concedes the collapse risk itself: A_xi is already 0.975 correlated with 1/mve, and if larger firms hold older longer-duration project stocks in equilibrium the new dimension folds back into size.

Cost: Jstar.csv must be regenerated once per type via the commented-out code at vasicek.py:123-174 (triple nested sum over 951 x 400 x 100 on an adaptive r grid), and again if BETA_ZR moves, since BETA_ZR enters the sigma12 recursion at vasicek.py:35-42 and hence B(k,r) and D(r). The kron work in sdf_compute_bgn.py terms 3/5/7 multiplies by M^2 = 9 on a moments step already pinned to n_jobs = 1 (config.py:40, because forked workers get OOM-killed). And the repo has a live precedent for exactly this failure mode: kp14's G_func.csv was solved under superseded parameters and is off by 49x, with kp14_fd.py unable to be re-run because `parameters_kp14` is missing from the repo.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: The proposer estimates DKKM/FM at 1.05-1.18x and I think that is optimistic. FM's span already contains any linear duration hedge; FF's size x payout double sort with value weighting recovers a coarse two-level version of the mix (the proposer admits this); and a firm holds only ~6 projects (my simulation: mean num 5.9, range 1-14), so its point on the 3-simplex is a 6-draw multinomial average - the mix is measured with enormous sampling error at the firm level, which caps how much ANY estimator, DKKM included, can recover. Meanwhile the unpriced-factor variance that the mix creates diversifies at 1/N. Expected realised movement in the DKKM/FF ratio: under 5%, for days of work and a solution-file regeneration with no correctness test.
verdicts.salvage: If duration heterogeneity is wanted for realism, get it for free without re-solving anything: heterogeneity in the SURVIVAL rate can be approximated by heterogeneity in the arrival/decay of exp(-beta_j) within the existing single-pi machinery, or simply add duration as a reported characteristic without changing the technology. But the honest recommendation is to spend the same engineering budget on making the existing cash-flow shock multi-dimensional and PRICED (see the P4 salvage), which requires no Jstar re-solve because the risk-neutral project value stays Chat*exp(-(beta_j + theta_m)), attacks the actual binding blocker (one priced shock, rank-1 price of risk, EffRank ~ 2), and costs one extra term in the eps construction at panel_functions_bgn.py:69-76.

missed_ideas: MAKE THE PRICED-RISK SPACE MULTI-DIMENSIONAL - the one change that attacks the actual binding blocker, and nobody proposed it. BGN has exactly one priced shock (log M = -r - 0.5*sigma_z^2 - sigma_z*nu) and a rank-1 price-of-risk vector; the measured EffRank of E[FF'] for this configuration is ~16 against the several hundred DKKM's AIPT calibration requires. Give each project a K-vector of factor loadings so cov(log M, log C_j) = -sum_k beta_jk*theta_k. The risk-neutral project value stays Chat*exp(-sum_k beta_jk*theta_k), so the exercise rule, Jstar.csv, integrand_optval and the beta calibration are ALL untouched - it is exactly as cheap as Proposal 1's one-line change. P4 gets 90% of the way to this and then deliberately makes the extra factors unpriced, which is the worthless version.

MEASUREMENT ERROR AND REPORTING LAGS ON THE CHARACTERISTICS, AS A PRIMARY LEVER. The diagnosis names this repeatedly ('the chars are noiseless, redundant, smooth, invertible functions of 2-3 latent states') and DKKM's own five-characteristic real-data experiment (FF6 0.74 -> 1.93-2.50) proves five chars suffice when they are noisy partial proxies. No proposal implements it directly. Minimal version: report book with a 1-2 quarter lag plus multiplicative noise, and supply 2-3 redundant noisy proxies of the same latent state with HETEROGENEOUS noise levels driven by an observable (firm age, history length). Optimal use of several noisy proxies with firm-specific reliability is a signal-dependent shrinkage problem - genuinely nonlinear, genuinely outside FM's linear span, and it requires no change to sdf_compute at all because the true moments are unaffected. This is strictly cheaper and safer than P2 and delivers P2's mechanism without the kappa surgery.

TIME-VARYING PRICE OF RISK INTERACTED WITH CHARACTERISTICS, EXPLOITING THE ONE CONDITIONING CHANNEL BGN ALREADY HAS. BGN has an observed macro state r_t, and dkkm_functions.rff line 96 already appends rf_stand raw to the RFF input for model=='bgn' - so DKKM alone can form char x macro-state interactions, while FF/FM never see rf at all (fama_functions._compute_monthly_fama passes only data[chars]). Make sigma_z or corr_zr a function of r_t so the cross-sectional premium on bm*betabar moves with the rate. Nobody proposed this. Two caveats that must be stated: (a) it is unfair by construction unless rf is added to FF/FM's information set too, and (b) the brief's own finding is that rf_stand is nearly annihilated by the second rank-standardization (65.6% of sin features are literally unchanged when rf_stand flips from -0.5 to +0.5), so this requires fixing dkkm_functions.py:110 to work at all.

A HEAVY-TAILED SIZE DISTRIBUTION / MICROCAP TAIL. DKKM's real-data Sharpe falls from 3.7 to ~1.6 in mega/large caps, so a large share of the empirical virtue of complexity is a microcap phenomenon. BGN's cross-section is far too compressed (num ranges 1-14, book = I*num is a small integer). Making the size distribution genuinely Pareto with strong size-dependence of BOTH alpha and idiosyncratic variance is a targeted, defensible change that no proposal makes, and unlike P1 it can be done with thin-tailed shocks so the conditional moments remain realisable in sample.

FIX THE FEATURE MAP'S INABILITY TO REPRESENT SPIKY WEIGHTS - this is a precondition for P1 and P5 that only P3's risk section mentions in passing. dkkm_functions.py:110 rank-standardizes the sin/cos features a second time, forcing every column to the identical bounded uniform marginal on [-0.5, 0.5]. No linear combination of such columns can be large on a small subset of firms. Every proposal whose true MVE weight is a ratio with a small denominator (P1's 1/d spanning 250-700x, P5's alpha/d) is handing DKKM a target its basis structurally cannot express. The fix is to replace the second rank-standardization with per-column standardization to unit variance - NOT to delete it (deleting it raises the linear-span share from 49% to 86% because it is the only thing equalising the 3x sin/cos amplitude asymmetry).

STOP USING POPULATION SPAN AS THE CEILING FOR DKKM - IT IS VACUOUS. Every proposal argues from 'basis X attains p% of max SR'. But at production N=1000 with D=3600 features, the RFF span is R^N and the population ceiling is 1.0 for any DGP. I confirmed this at N=250: RFF as configured with D=360 attains 1.0000 of max at both band settings, and even D=36 attains 0.914-0.951 at m=1.75. So no proposal's 'DKKM ceiling' number is informative; the entire question is estimation efficiency at T=360. The right pre-implementation diagnostic is a small Monte Carlo of the ACTUAL estimators (real rank_standardize/rff/ridge_regr code paths, T=360 rolling window) evaluated against the true rp and Sigma - which is cheap, and which none of the six proposals ran.

CHECK THAT THE TRUE CONDITIONAL MOMENTS ARE REALISABLE IN SAMPLE - a guard nobody proposed and which P1 fails badly. At the proposed band, mean diag(cond_var) is 0.03733 while the average realised cross-sectional variance over 59 months is 0.00482, a factor of 7.7. Any model change should be required to satisfy mean(diag(cond_var)) ~ mean realised cross-sectional variance to within ~25%, and realised excess kurtosis in single digits. Otherwise the metric grades the estimator against tail moments its 360-month training sample never displays, and every method fails for reasons unrelated to complexity.

EXPLOIT FF'S VALUE WEIGHTING RATHER THAN IGNORING IT. fama_french value-weights inside all six cells (fama_functions.py:88-93) and mkt_rf = mve/mve.sum() (line 115), so FF's weight space is {mve_i x step function of chars} - already nonlinear in characteristics. Any proposal whose true w* is proportional to mve times a smooth function of chars is partly free for FF. Proposals should be screened by checking that the target w* is orthogonal to the span of {mve x cell indicators}, which none of the six did; my FF-style basis attains 0.64-0.71 of max at the proposed P1 calibration, well above the 0.36-0.50 the diagnosis brief implies.

REPORT max_sr AND Sharpe/max_sr. max_sr is already computed in every sdf_loop (sdf_compute_bgn.py:326-328) and saved into *_moments.pkl by calculate_moments.py, but evaluate_sdfs.py never propagates it, so no table shows it. Without it none of these six proposals can be evaluated: 'FF at 0.2423' is uninterpretable until you know whether max_sr is 0.26 or 2.6. This is a zero-risk measurement fix that should precede every model change, and it is the single cheapest thing on this list.
